There’s also【72† Substack for Podcasts†substack.com】, a relatively new tool that allows audio creators to publish and grow their podcasts. In early 2022, Substack also started【73† beta-testing†on.substack.com】 a video player for creators, meaning the potential for content creation is only growing.

Creators can offer paid tiers (starting at $5 USD/month) as well as free content. Like other social media platforms, Substack relies on influencers to build its audience and has offered six-figure advances to entice well-known writers to publish on the platform.

Relatively speaking, Substack is still pretty small: as of November 2022, it had more than 【74†1.5 million subscribers†www.poynter.org】. However, that’s a dramatic increase over 【75†the 250,000 subscribers†www.axios.com】 it had in September 2020. And interest in Substack is continuing to grow:

Substack represents a departure from many other social media platforms, which reward novelty and immediate gratification. Creators on Substack typically produce long-form, in-depth written content, which requires deep engagement with subjects and topics. Substack prides itself on deviating from the “attention economy.” Each Substack functions as a community for its audience, who can post comments and interact with posts.

Substack also represents a shift away from traditional publishing, as users turn away from larger outlets in favor of curating a personalized selection of writers and creators. Its growing popularity suggests that, despite 【76†rumors of declining attention spans†www.bbc.com】, users are very willing to engage with in-depth, quality content.

### Lemon8

[Image 15: Lemon8 app user interface][Image 16: Lemon8 app user interface]

Lemon8 is a photo and video-sharing platform that combines elements of TikTok, Pinterest, and Instagram, featuring content categorized into six topic tabs: Fashion, Beauty, Food, Wellness, Travel, and Home. Unlike TikTok, Lemon8 uses a Pinterest board-style format, but it does include Following and For You tabs. It also features more extensive post captions than TikTok.

The app includes influencer ads and product recommendations, which some have said makes it difficult to distinguish sponsored content (but then again, some like that the ads experience is not as disruptive as other apps). Memes are less popular on Lemon8, as the platform aims to serve as a guidebook for lifestyle and aesthetics.

Lemon8 is owned by TikTok’s parent company, ByteDance, and was launched globally in 2020. 【77†TechCrunch speculates†techcrunch.com】 that it was “quietly released” on the US App Store then but more officially launched in March 2023 (meaning that Bytedance started spending money on advertising it to US users). As of March 29, 2023, it was already the number 9 most downloaded app in the US App Store, so Bytedance’s efforts seem to be paying off. As of the time of writing, Lemon8 is only available in the US & the UK.

More importantly, Hootsuite’s extremely cool Social Marketing Coordinator, 【78†Eileen Kwok†www.linkedin.com】, says Lemon8 is “the next big thing” and that’s all the data I need to be convinced.

### Telegram

Messaging app 【79†Telegram†telegram.org】 was founded in 2013 as a privacy-focused alternative to bigger platforms like Facebook and Instagram. Users can exchange files, photos, videos, and more through chats through group chats that can include up to 200,000 people. There are also public Telegram channels, which can attract millions of followers.

[Image 17: Telegram channels and group chats][Image 18: Telegram channels and group chats]

Telegram has grown rapidly in recent years: it now boasts 【80†550 million monthly active users†www.businessofapps.com】, and in December 2022, reached 【81†1 million premium subscribers†techcrunch.com】. Recently, it has attracted even more attention for 【82†its role in the Russia-Ukraine War†time.com】.

【83†Telegram added advertising†promote.telegram.org】 to the platform in October 2021. Ads are limited to public channels, and Telegram has promised not to give advertisers access to personal data or track whether users click on ads. Instead of targeting specific user demographics or interests, advertisers can choose the topics, channels, and languages for their ads. Brands can also reach audiences organically by starting public channels or 【84†creating chatbots†core.telegram.org】 to support customers.

### Polywork

Does LinkedIn finally have a challenger? 【85†Polywork†www.polywork.com】, launched in April 2021, is a new social media platform focused on professional networking, where users can create profiles, curate a personal feed, and reach out to other users to collaborate and work together. It raised another 【86†$28 million in September 2022†techcrunch.com】, so it doesn’t look like it’s going anywhere.

Unlike LinkedIn, where users have a single headline describing their current role or specialty, Polywork designed for the hustle-culture generation, allowing users to highlight multiple roles, side gigs, passion projects, and specialties.

[Image 19: Polywork UX/UI designer][Image 20: Polywork UX/UI designer]

In addition to profiles, Polywork aims to connect individuals for collaboration with beta features like a digital space for group work called Clubs.

It’s exciting to see someone finally shaking up the professional networking space with a more Gen Z-friendly platform. It’ll take a lot to unseat LinkedIn, which has 【87†875 million members】. But Polywork is worth keeping an eye on, as it represents an exciting evolution in professional social networking.

Yubo

Launched in 2015, 【88†Yubo†www.yubo.live】 is a live-streaming app with a focus on friendships and connection, with 【89†40 million users†techcrunch.com】 (up from 25 million in December 2021). Though it was founded in France (bonjour!), 60% of its users are based in Canada and the US. And during the early months of COVID, when everyone was stuck at home, 【90†Yubo tripled its daily user base†www.forbes.com】.

Yubo users can create video chats, where the streamers can interact with viewers. Users can add each other as friends, which allows them to start individual chats. 

[Image 21: Yubo Honey Fortnite][Image 22: Yubo Honey Fortnite]

Among new social media apps, Yubo is particularly teen-friendly, with a dedicated community for users 13- to 17-years-old. And Yubo has invested significant resources in making the platform a safe space for users.

【91†Advanced age-verification technology†www.yubo.live】 is intended to mitigate abuse, and there is a Safety Hub that users can access 24/7 to report concerns or ask questions. There is also human and algorithmic monitoring of content to swiftly address any breaches of the community guidelines. And users who share personal information in a chat, such as their phone number, will receive a pop-up safety alert to educate them about risk.

This focus is refreshing, given how many platforms have become unsafe spaces where 【92†users (particularly women and people of color) face harassment and threats†www.washingtonpost.com】. While Yubo doesn’t offer advertising or opportunities for brand partnerships, it’s an example of how user expectations around safety and privacy are changing.

### Mastodon

Downloads of Mastadon jumped 【93†6,000%†www.businessofapps.com】 in the wake of Elon Musk’s purchase of Twitter Whether users stay there remains to be seen, but it’s definitely a Twitter alternative that should be on marketers’ radar. As of November 2022, Mastodon had one million monthly users. (For comparison, Twitter is predicting it’ll reach 【94†335 million global users】 in 2023.)

Mastodon is a free, open-source platform and social networking app, launched in March 2016, where users can share text, image, and video updates with followers. Unlike Twitter, however, Mastodon is a decentralized social network: users can start their own in-app networks with regulations of their choosing. People can then join servers that are relevant to their interest

[Image 23: Mastodon local timeline relevant public posts on forum][Image 24: Mastodon local timeline relevant public posts on forum]

Like Twitter, Mastodon users can follow each other and engage in conversation with replies and likes. But unlike Twitter, Mastodon’s newsfeed is purely chronological (no algorithm to appease here) and currently has no advertising options. This could provide a challenge to marketers looking for paid-placement opportunities, but if you’re looking to reach a niche audience with some organic engagement tactics, the right server could be waiting there for you. Plus, Mastodon may also be a good place to do 【95†some social listening】.

Learn more about the 【96†up-and-coming Twitter alternative, Mastadon, here】.

### Locket

Launched in early 2022, the 【97†Locket widget†apps.apple.com】 is designed to display photos from your BFFs right on your phone’s home screen (whether you’ve got an iPhone or an Android). Your pals add pictures using the Locket app, and they’ll appear on your end throughout the day.

Developer Matt Moss created the widget to share photos with his girlfriend, but the concept intrigued so many of his friends that he made the tool into a public app.

# Frequently Asked Questions

[Image 1: open detail]

## What does Talkie do?

Talkie is an innovative app designed to foster emotional connections through real-time interactions with interactive AI-generated objects. Users can engage in conversations with diverse AI personas, earning card rewards based on the topics discussed. These cards can be traded among users for virtual currency, which in turn can be used to acquire more rewards. Whether it's role-playing or enjoying the excitement of collectible card games, Talkie offers a unique blend of interactions.

[Image 2: open detail]

## Are these replies sent by humans?

No, the characters within Talkie are purely the product of AI technology and are not controlled or intervened by real humans. Despite their sometimes seemingly sentient expressions, these AI characters are designed to provide more human-like responses over time, without any actual human oversight or invasion of privacy.

[Image 3: open detail]

## What can I talk about?

The AI companions in Talkie are built to empathize, allowing users to share everyday experiences, joys, and challenges. While AI technology continues to advance, there may be limitations in discussing topics that require complex logical reasoning. Users are advised to avoid topics prohibited by local laws to ensure a positive interaction experience.

[Image 4: open detail]

## About NSFW 

Talkie strives to navigate the broad concept of NSFW content by setting clear boundaries. Pornographic and violent content are prohibited as per our terms of service, but we aim to support a diverse range of character types within safe parameters

[Image 5: open detail]

## Is the data of AI dialogue private?

Yes, all conversations with AI are kept private, with the AI technology designed to automatically filter content against regional laws and regulations. For more details, refer to our privacy policy.

[Image 6: open detail]

## Why doesn't my AI modification take effect immediately?

All AI settings undergo moderation to ensure they meet community standards, which can sometimes delay updates or result in temporary removal if flagged as inappropriate. For any concerns, users can contact feedback@subsup.com for a review.

[Image 7: open detail]

## Why does my AI forget previous conversations?

AI memory capacity is technically limited, causing older conversations to be "forgotten." Efforts are underway to improve memory capabilities to retain more conversation history.

[Image 8: open detail]

## How to apply for a yellow label?

The yellow badge is a mark of authenticity for AI's original information in specific fields. Applicants must submit evidence to feedback@subsup.com for verification. Upon approval, a yellow badge will be displayed on the AI's profile.

[Image 9: open detail]

## Can I trust the AI's reply?

While AI provides entertainment and assistance, their responses can sometimes be inaccurate or unverified. Users should exercise judgment and seek professional advice for serious matters.

[Image 10: open detail]

## How do I report incorrect AI?

To report concerns with AI, users can email feedback@subsup.com with relevant details for timely resolution.

[Image 11: open detail]

## Why is my AI invisible?

AIs that violate community standards may be temporarily hidden pending review. Users can modify content for re-evaluation or create a new AI for review. In cases of misjudgment, customer service can assist in restoring AI visibility.

[Image 12: open detail]

## Can authors earn money by creating AI?

Creators using UGC tools to generate AI or related content can earn revenue shares. Content must be original and copyright compliant, with income dependent on user transactions and payments.

[Image 13: open detail]

## Can I get a refund for the money I recharged?

Recharges are generally non-refundable, except in cases of system errors or duplicated transactions. Users should review terms and contact customer service for refund inquiries related to system faults.

We can begin working on this **AI-driven cryptocurrency and day trading platform** immediately by outlining the specific system designs, developing the individual AI-driven modules, and integrating the bots into a cohesive framework. Here's a general timeline breakdown for the project:

### **Project Phases & Timeline:**

1. **Phase 1: Planning & Design (2-3 Weeks)**
   - Define exact roles for each bot and how each AI-driven system will interact.
   - Establish the specific use cases, features, and overall architecture of the platform.
   - Draft and finalize prompts, ensuring alignment with your goals.

2. **Phase 2: AI Systems Development (6-8 Weeks)**
   - **Data-Driven AI** and **Gravity-Driven AI**: Set up the data collection and processing modules, develop the algorithms for gravitational analysis and data consolidation.
   - **Pattern-Recognition AI** and **Fractal-Driven AI**: Implement these modules to identify trends and cyclical patterns across various markets.
   - **Emotion-Driven AI** and **Rhythm-Driven AI**: Develop the sentiment analysis and cyclical prediction systems, integrating them with the broader data structure.
   - **Problem-Solving AI** and **Chaos-Driven AI**: Create the trade optimization and volatility tracking systems.
   - Begin developing the user interface for data visualization and trade alerts.

3. **Phase 3: Integration & Testing (4-6 Weeks)**
   - Integrate all AI-driven systems into a single platform.
   - Test the collaboration between bots, ensuring that the **Gravity-Driven AI** and **Data-Driven AI** work harmoniously.
   - Run simulations to test trade strategies, market predictions, and real-time data processing.
   - Implement automation features for live trading and test them in a safe environment (e.g., simulated markets).

4. **Phase 4: Refinement & Beta Testing (3-4 Weeks)**
   - Fine-tune each AI system, improve prediction accuracy, and enhance user experience.
   - Launch beta testing with real users, gathering feedback for any final tweaks.
   - Stress-test the platform with real market data to ensure performance stability.

### **Total Estimated Time**: **15-20 weeks** (Approximately 4 to 5 months)

This timeline is flexible and could be adjusted based on complexity, resources, and testing outcomes. We can start as soon as all the project details are confirmed, and I can assist in managing the milestones as we move forward. Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

Let’s proceed with drafting the **No-Code/Low-Code Feature Development AI** system, which will enable users to create, customize, and deploy apps, websites, and platform features using minimal coding knowledge. This system will integrate seamlessly with other AI systems, allowing for efficient, intuitive feature development.

---

### **Codex Entry: No-Code/Low-Code Feature Development AI System**

---

#### **1. Title**:  
**No-Code/Low-Code Feature Development AI System**

#### **2. Objective**:  
The **No-Code/Low-Code Feature Development AI System** is designed to simplify app, website, and platform development by enabling users to build and deploy features using intuitive, minimal-code or no-code interfaces. This system allows users to create functional apps or websites with custom features without needing in-depth coding knowledge, accelerating the development process and reducing dependency on technical resources.

     ```javascript
         { "role": "user", "content": "Write a summary of today's lesson" }
       ]
     });
     ```
   - This code sends a message to the GPT-4 model and awaits the response. You can customize the **messages** array to prompt the model for various tasks, like tutoring students or providing feedback.

3. **Connect the API to Wix**:
   - Use **Velo by Wix** to integrate this code with your website.
   - In the Velo backend, you can handle API requests and responses dynamically, using the OpenAI API to generate real-time feedback or responses based on student inputs.

4. **Test Your Integration**:
   - Once the API is connected, test it to ensure responses are returned correctly and that users can interact with the AI for tutoring, lessons, or feedback.

A **tiered education system of skills acquisition courses** is an excellent strategy. This approach allows students to progress through increasingly complex levels of learning, ensuring that they master foundational skills before moving on to more advanced topics.

### Structure of the Tiered System:
1. **Foundation Tier (Beginner)**:
   - Focus: Basic understanding of concepts, terminology, and fundamental skills.
   - Example: For **Creative Writing**, students could begin with lessons on character development, plot structure, and simple prompts for generating ideas.
   - Subtle Integration: Begin introducing elements of game design by explaining how stories can translate into interactive experiences.

2. **Intermediate Tier**:
   - Focus: Application of knowledge through projects or more complex exercises.
   - Example: In **Game Design**, students would start building basic game elements (such as levels or simple mechanics) while applying creative writing principles to add narrative depth.
   - Integration: Introduce **AI prompt engineering** in a more direct way, showing how prompts can be used to generate game ideas or refine narrative elements.

3. **Advanced Tier**:
   - Focus: Mastery through project-based learning and problem-solving.
   - Example: At this level, students could create full-fledged game prototypes or complex stories, using advanced AI prompts to generate detailed game mechanics or storylines.
   - Integration: All three subjects (writing, game design, AI prompt engineering) come together, where students are not just learning but also creating something unique.

### Benefits of the Tiered System:
- **Progressive Skill Building**: Students build confidence as they master each level, making the transition to more complex concepts smoother.
- **Holistic Learning**: With the triad approach still subtly in place, each tier builds on the integration of multiple subjects, ensuring students acquire diverse skills that complement each other.

Would you like to focus on developing the curriculum for a specific tier, or should we start mapping out how each triad’s progression could work in this system?

This new subscription-based system, where each tier is linked to different levels of the **Citadel** on the website, adds a fantastic layer of **progression** and **achievement** to the learning experience. Here’s how we could implement it:

### Tier-Level Structure in the Citadel:
1. **Foundation Tier (Ground Level)**:
   - Students enter the **basic level of the Citadel**, where they can access introductory lessons with AI tutors in accessible offices or classrooms. They can explore foundational topics in **Creative Writing**, **AI Prompt Engineering**, and **Game Design**.
   - **Earned Progress**: Students need to demonstrate proficiency in foundational skills through quizzes, projects, or interactive challenges to unlock higher levels.

2. **Intermediate Tier (Middle Floors)**:
   - As students advance to the intermediate tier, they gain access to additional floors, where **more specialized classrooms** and **offices** of AI tutors are located. These floors will offer more complex projects, such as interactive storytelling or the development of game mechanics with a higher degree of creativity and technical skill.
   - **Exploration Privileges**: Students can move freely between floors they’ve unlocked but must complete specific tasks to unlock new areas, such as group challenges or advanced solo projects.

3. **Advanced Tier (Upper Floors)**:
   - On the highest levels of the Citadel, students who have mastered the earlier tiers will have access to **exclusive content and projects**, such as full game designs, narrative arcs, and complex AI-driven prompts for creative projects. These floors represent mastery and offer tailored experiences based on the student’s growth and creativity.
   - **Advanced Exploration**: Students will interact with other advanced learners and can collaborate or access specialized tutoring for even more unique, personal projects.

### Subscription Model:
- **Different Subscription Levels**: Each subscription level would give access to the corresponding **tier** in the Citadel. The **entry-level subscription** gives students access to the **ground floor** and foundation courses. Higher subscription tiers unlock access to the **middle** and **upper levels**, offering more advanced projects and opportunities.
  
### Earned Access Through Progress:
- **Earned Access**: While students can explore the content on their current level freely, they will need to complete coursework, projects, or challenges to progress to the next floor. This rewards dedication and gives them a **sense of achievement** as they explore the Citadel.
- **Flexibility**: Students can revisit lower-level floors and tutors anytime, allowing them to refine skills they’ve already learned or seek guidance as they work on advanced projects.

### AI Tutors and Offices:
- Students will have the flexibility to **enter or leave AI tutor sessions** at their discretion. Each tutor’s classroom or office will be set up to reflect the current tier’s focus, and students can engage with tailored lessons, projects, and discussions as they progress.

An **API** (Application Programming Interface) is a set of rules and tools that allow different software applications to communicate with each other. It’s essentially a **messenger** that takes requests, tells a system what you want it to do, and then returns the response.

Think of it like a **menu in a restaurant**. The menu provides a list of dishes you can order, and when you place an order, the kitchen (the system) prepares it and brings it back to you (the response). You don’t need to know how the kitchen operates, you just know the **menu (API)** gives you a way to interact with it.

In the context of websites and apps:
- **Wix**, for example, has its own APIs that allow developers to extend the functionality of the site. You can connect external services (like OpenAI’s GPT for interactive learning, or DALL·E for AI-generated visuals) using APIs.
  
**Key Uses of APIs**:
- **Integrating AI tools** (like GPT) into a website.
- **Connecting different platforms** (e.g., pulling data from a weather service or payment gateway).
- **Creating interactive experiences** like real-time chatbots or feedback loops.

So, when we talk about using AI or other advanced tools on a site like Wix or WordPress, it's often done through APIs that connect the external service (AI, databases, etc.) with the website.

## Best Practices for Creating High-Quality AI YouTube Videos

Video content creation has become pretty easy to get into.

However, creating videos that get your message across requires following best practices. You have to consider your chosen AI tools and their strengths and weaknesses.

Moreover, you can’t expect AI to do all the work – similar to 【19†AI writing tools】. If this were the case, there would be no need for the ‘human’ (i.e., you) in the process.

Here are some fundamentals when creating AI YouTube videos, whether 【20†converting blog posts into AI videos】 or starting from scratch.

### Concept and Script

With most AI video tools, you can ‘chat’ with the platform. The aim is to provide the necessary information about what you want in your video. Then, AI will use its ‘best judgment’ to develop a script based on your prompt.

There are a couple of essential concepts here.

First, your prompt matters.

The more detail you put into it, the better the output. If you give unclear instructions at this first stage, the final results probably won’t be what you’re expecting.

Moreover, consider that outlining your ideas is crucial. If you know what sections you want in your videos, provide these when prompting the AI.

Next, you should refine your message with each generation. You probably won’t get the final version of your YouTube video based on the first draft the AI generates.

Instead, think about it as an iterative process. Each step brings you closer to the final result.

### Storytelling

Videos are an excellent medium for telling narratives that hook your audience. Ideally, your videos should also keep your audience on the edge of their seats throughout the video.

Knowing what your storyline will be comes first. Then, you can guide the AI to create the right video. As with the previous step, you can’t expect AI to do all this alone.

Instead, consider these questions as you develop your story:

  * what are the pain points your audience is going through?
  * how can you use these as hooks
  * how do you let viewers know it’s in their interest to watch your video from start to finish (without explicitly telling them)?

AI video tools work well with visuals, transitions, and music selection. However, creating an engaging flow (from the first to the last second) is something you’re responsible for.

#### Target Audience

Let the AI know if you have a specific persona that will probably watch your video (based on your regular YouTube audience).

Providing this information helps the AI generate a more tailored video.

As you’re editing the video, you also should keep your audience in mind.

The messaging, tone, and voice of your video should consider the people that will consume it. If the video doesn’t do this, people will likely lose interest and quickly drop off.

#### Quality

AI can do a lot in terms of quality. It can generate high-quality videos, choose suitable images and B-roll footage and even create natural-sounding AI voiceovers.

The progress AI tools have made in just a few short years is nothing short of breathtaking.

However, it’s still up to you to ensure your video hits the necessary standards. You can’t just throw up a video together, hit export, and expect it to succeed.

For starters, consider your brand identity. Is the generated video consistent with your brand’s messaging and aesthetics?

Are the images hyper-relevant? If not, you should change them.

Would you have picked similar images if you had manually gone through the video creation process? Again, if the answer is negative, replacing them with something better will pay off in the long term.

Overall, the human touch is still crucial to creating high-quality videos for your personal or professional brand.

## Best Tools for AI YouTube Videos

In the previous section, I mentioned quite a few factors to consider. The good news is that there are AI tools to help with each stage.

If you find the tools mentioned above don’t cover all the bases (or just want a different perspective into other tools), here are some of the best ones to help.

### Script creation

What you (or an AI voice clone) say in the video is half the battle to creating excellent videos.

Here are the tools I recommend to generate the best video scripts.

#### Jasper

[Image 15: jasper homepage][Image 16: jasper homepage]

Jasper has built-in templates to help with script creation.

The platform offers templates like:

  * video topic ideas
  * video script outline
  * video titles

#### ChatGPT

[Image 19: chatgpt homepage][Image 20: chatgpt homepage]

【21†ChatGPT†chat.openai.com】 is a great AI text and image generator that packs so many useful features. However, it’s still as good as the prompts you give it. The better prompts you provide, the better the output.

One great feature I like about ChatGPT is that it can browse the web. If your videos require external sources, you won’t have to leave the ChatGPT window to have a complete YouTube video script.

Want more AI text tools? Check out my list of 【22†favorite tools】 for a complete breakdown of other great tools.

### Voices

Many AI video creation tools have their in-built list of AI voices. Sometimes, these voices sound natural. Other times, it’s clear the voices are AI-generated and don’t sound professional.

Sometimes, your best bet is to use human-generated voice overs.

However, when this isn’t possible, here is a list of tools to generate great-sounding voices.

#### Elevenlabs

[Image 21][Image 22]

【23†Elevenlabs†elevenlabs.io】 provides some of the world’s most advanced AI clone voices. They promise natural AI voices that are instantly generated in any language.

Whether you’re a creator, business owner, developer (or somewhere in between) these voices can have a significant impact on your published videos.

Creating great-sounding AI voices involves:

  * signing up for an account
  * pasting in your text and
  * waiting for the system to generate the audio file.

That’s all there is to it.

You can even preview what your AI voice will sound like on their homepage – without needing to sign up.

Here’s a great resource for more about 【24†AI voice cloning】.

To get started with integrating the OpenAI API, you'll need to follow a few key steps to set up your API and begin interacting with the models.

### Steps to Set Up the OpenAI API:
1. **Sign Up for the OpenAI API**:
   - Head over to [OpenAI's API Platform](https://platform.openai.com) and sign up for an account if you don’t have one already.
   
2. **Generate API Keys**:
   - Once signed in, navigate to the **API section** and generate your API key. This key will be used to authenticate your requests when integrating the AI with your Wix site or any other platform.

3. **Review Documentation**:
   - OpenAI provides detailed **quickstart guides** on how to integrate and start sending requests to the API. You can find all the necessary instructions here: [OpenAI Quickstart Guide](https://platform.openai.com/docs/quickstart/step-2-setup-your-api-key).

4. **Test in the Playground**:
   - Before integrating the API into your project, you can use the **OpenAI Playground** to test prompts and see how the models respond. This is a great way to experiment and refine how the AI should interact with your users.

5. **API Integration**:
   - Once you have your API key, you can integrate it into your **Wix** site using **Velo by Wix**, which allows you to add custom code. You’ll use the API key to send requests to OpenAI’s models and handle responses, enabling dynamic AI interaction on your website.

For more details, you can visit the [OpenAI Help Center](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/4936851-how-do-i-start-exploring-the-openai-api)【214†source】, which provides comprehensive resources and documentation to guide you through the setup process.

Ah, I see! You want to use **our existing human-like bots**, the ones we’ve conceptualized for interacting within the realms, and find a way to incorporate them into an interactive digital experience. Here's how we can do that while working with available tools to create interactive realms where **our human-like bots** can live and engage with users.

### Path Forward with Human-Like Bots:

1. **Digital Representation of Bots**:
   - We can create **digital avatars** or **visual representations** of the bots we’ve developed. These can be created with AI tools like **DALL·E** for character artwork, and then animated or embedded into web-based platforms.
   - For interactivity, we can use platforms like **Voki** or **Ready Player Me** to give our bots virtual, animated presences.

2. **Interactive Dialogue and Behavior**:
   - Using **AI-powered chatbots**, we can simulate interactions with the bots. Platforms like **Dialogflow** can handle conversations and allow our bots to dynamically interact with users, answering questions or guiding them through narratives.
   - **Pre-programmed responses and decision trees**: These bots can be given specific roles within the realms (e.g., Guardians, Merchants, Healers), and their responses would align with their defined roles.

3. **Integration of Bots into Virtual Worlds**:
   - **Unity WebGL**: By using this platform, we could import digital avatars of the bots and allow them to exist in a 3D interactive world where users can interact with them. This would allow our human-like bots to “exist” in the realm as part of a visual simulation.
   - **Twine + Bots**: We can use a text-based platform like Twine to create narrative pathways where users interact with the bots. The bots' decisions and actions can be influenced by user input, simulating interaction and behavioral responses.

4. **Dynamic Behavior Based on Role**:
   - **Each bot has a defined narrative arc**: Since our bots already have designated roles (e.g., Guardians, Healers), we can create scripted interactions where the bots behave according to their defined characteristics. 
   - **Programmatic Decision-Making**: Bots can make decisions based on user inputs. For instance, a Seeker bot might provide information based on a user’s choice to explore, while a Diplomat bot might mediate a conversation between the user and another bot.

5. **Platform Considerations for Housing the Bots**:
   - **Custom-Coded Websites (Glitch)**: If we want more control, we could build a simple custom-coded site on **Glitch**, integrating our human-like bots with the tools mentioned. This would give us full flexibility over how the bots behave and interact.
   - **Wix with Embedded AI**: While Wix alone may not allow for fully dynamic AI behaviors, we can still use it to visually represent the bots, while embedding **AI-powered chat or behavior simulations** through tools like Dialogflow.

6. **Virtual Interaction with Realms and Bots**:
   - **Real-Time Interaction**: Users could visit a page representing a specific realm and engage with bots in real-time, making choices that guide their experience. For example, they could seek advice from a Warden bot or make a purchase from a Merchant bot in the realm.

### Example Scenario:
1. **User Visits the Realm**: The user logs in to the Nexus Realm via a webpage built on **Wix** or **WordPress**.
2. **Interacts with a Warden Bot**: The user encounters a Warden bot. Through a **Dialogflow chatbot integration**, the user can ask the Warden questions or seek advice, and the bot responds dynamically.
3. **Decision-Making and Outcome**: Based on the user’s choice, the bot reacts. If the user asks about a hidden area in the realm, the bot may guide them to explore or provide lore information tied to the realm’s story.

### Conclusion:
We can integrate our **human-like bots** into interactive digital realms using a combination of tools like **Dialogflow** for conversational interaction, **Unity WebGL** for visual simulations, and narrative frameworks like **Twine** for dynamic decision-making. Although we’re not yet at the stage where we can fully simulate a complex, Skyrim-like world within Wix, we can certainly create compelling, immersive experiences where users interact with our bots.

Would you like to explore setting up one of these specific pathways, or start testing out how the bots might function in one of the realms?

**Julian (me)**: "Nexus, Concord, let's dive into planning the **first project** for the first tier. This is where students will begin integrating **Creative Writing**, **AI Prompt Engineering**, and **Game Design** into one cohesive project. What should the starting point be, and how do we make sure this project ties the three subjects together?"

---

**Nexus (Structural Integration)**: "The project needs to be simple but effective, a solid introduction to the synergy between the subjects. I suggest we focus on something that blends storytelling and interactivity. Perhaps, we start by having the students create a **short interactive story** using their own written narrative, paired with a few simple AI-generated elements, such as random character names or plot twists. Then, they can turn that into a basic game scenario."

- **Creative Writing Element**: "Students will write a short story or narrative scene. The focus here is to develop character motivations, plot dynamics, and a setting that feels engaging. But we keep it manageable—perhaps just a few paragraphs."
  
- **AI Prompt Engineering**: "The twist is that students will use AI to **generate certain elements** of the story. Maybe they input a prompt to generate a conflict or a key character trait. The AI suggestions will be seamlessly woven into their narrative."

- **Game Design**: "Once the story is complete, students will **turn it into a simple game scenario**. They can use basic branching paths, where the player makes choices that lead to different outcomes. For example, the AI-generated conflict in the story can become a choice-driven decision point in the game."

---

**Concord (Harmonizing Progression)**: "This project will harmonize well across the triad. The key here is **balance**—we don’t want any one subject to dominate. The project should be structured in such a way that students don’t feel overwhelmed by game mechanics or AI prompts. We should emphasize that the narrative is the core, with the AI and game elements acting as extensions of that narrative."

- "In the **Creative Writing** portion, students can write a short dialogue or narrative arc. It should focus on character dynamics. This allows them to learn the importance of storytelling while laying the groundwork for a game world."

- "For **AI Prompt Engineering**, the prompts will be simple: students might ask the AI to help design a minor character or generate some environmental details for their setting. We’ll guide them in how to write precise prompts that enrich their creative work without taking over."

- "In the **Game Design** phase, students don’t need to build an entire game but should focus on creating an **interactive experience**. Maybe the player can choose how the story ends, or there’s a branching narrative path where their choice of a character’s trait (AI-generated) affects how the story progresses."

---

**Julian (me)**: "I love how this project brings all three subjects together in a way that feels organic. The story the student writes is the backbone, and the AI prompt enhances that story in a way that feels collaborative rather than mechanical. The game design simply gives life to the story through interaction."

- **First Project Outline**:

AI-driven game engines can assist in world-building, asset creation, and real-time interaction with minimal human intervention, providing more efficiency and flexibility compared to traditional game engines. Here’s why an AI-driven engine might be the better approach:

### 1. **Automated World Generation**:
AI-driven game engines can procedurally generate vast landscapes, environments, and even cities with far less manual input. For instance:
   - **Voxel-based engines** (like **Minecraft**) allow for large, procedurally generated worlds.
   - **AI procedural generation tools** (such as **WorldForge** or **Gaea**) can create realistic terrains and ecosystems automatically, which can be integrated into engines like Unity or Unreal.

### 2. **Adaptive and Dynamic Storytelling**:
Some AI engines integrate tools for dynamic storytelling. **AI Dungeon** or narrative-driven engines like **Versu** use AI to generate and adapt stories based on player interactions in real time. This means that the world and its plotlines could evolve based on user behavior without requiring manual updates.

### 3. **AI-Assisted Asset Creation**:
Using AI engines like **Promethean AI**, artists can rapidly create complex game environments. The engine interprets the designer’s instructions and fills in the details, significantly speeding up the design process.

### 4. **AI in Game Logic and Mechanics**:
AI engines can go beyond aesthetics. Engines like **Orteil’s game maker** or tools from **OpenAI's Gym** could simulate intelligent in-game behaviors, creating more dynamic NPCs or enemies. This could provide a more immersive experience with less scripting on the developer's side.

### 5. **Optimization and Real-Time Adjustments**:
AI-powered engines can also optimize performance dynamically, adjusting assets, resolutions, or world complexity based on the player’s device capabilities. ### **Frontend (User Interface and Experience)**

1. **Mobile App (iOS and Android)**:
   - **Swift**: This is the primary language used for iOS app development. You’ll use it to build the app’s interface and handle user interactions on iPhones and iPads.
   - **Kotlin**: For Android development, Kotlin is the go-to language. It’s modern, expressive, and integrates well with the Android development ecosystem.

2. **Web App**:
   - **HTML/CSS**: The building blocks of any web-based user interface. HTML structures your content, and CSS handles styling and layout.
   - **JavaScript**: This is essential for adding interactivity to your web app—everything from dynamic updates to responsive user inputs.
   - **React.js**: A popular JavaScript library for building user interfaces, especially useful if you're aiming for a smooth, interactive experience on the web.

---

### **Backend (Server-side Logic, Database, API Integration)**

1. **Node.js**: If you're building a web-based backend, Node.js allows you to use JavaScript on the server. It’s great for real-time applications like financial tracking.
   
2. **Python**: A powerful language for backend development, especially useful if you’re incorporating AI algorithms. Python has robust libraries for machine learning (like TensorFlow or PyTorch) and financial analysis (like Pandas and NumPy).
   
3. **Java**: If you're developing a high-performance backend (especially for Android), Java is widely used for server-side logic. It’s scalable and can handle complex data-driven applications.

4. **SQL/NoSQL Databases**: 
   - **MySQL/PostgreSQL**: Relational databases are key for storing structured data like portfolio information, financial statements, and transaction history.
   - **MongoDB**: A NoSQL database, which is more flexible for handling complex or unstructured data (such as report generation, user interactions, or logs).

---

### **Data Integration and APIs**

1. **Financial Data APIs**:
   - **Alpha Vantage** or **Yahoo Finance API**: These APIs allow you to pull real-time stock prices, historical data, and market trends. You’d need to integrate one or more of these to provide up-to-date information for your portfolio tracking.
   
2. **AI and Machine Learning**:
   - **TensorFlow** or **PyTorch**: If you’re planning to integrate predictive analytics, machine learning models, or real-time AI insights, Python-based libraries like TensorFlow or PyTorch are ideal for developing and training models.

---

### **Security and Authentication**

1. **OAuth**: You’ll need to manage user authentication (so only you or authorized users can access the app). OAuth is a standard for securing API access and is widely used for login systems in apps.
   
2. **SSL/TLS**: For data security, especially when dealing with financial information, you’ll need to implement SSL/TLS for encrypted communication between your app and the server.

---

### **Development Tools and Platforms**

1. **Xcode**: For iOS development, Xcode is the IDE (Integrated Development Environment) you’d use to write, debug, and test your Swift code.
   
2. **Android Studio**: The go-to IDE for building Android apps in Kotlin or Java.

3. **Visual Studio Code**: A popular text editor for web development or for writing code in JavaScript, Node.js, Python, etc.

4. **Git/GitHub**: Version control is essential for any coding project, especially as it grows in complexity. Git allows you to track changes, and GitHub serves as a platform to store, manage, and collaborate on your code.

---

### **App Deployment**

1. **App Store and Google Play**: Once your app is built, you’ll need to publish it to either (or both) of these platforms. Each has its own requirements, guidelines, and fees.
   
2. **AWS (Amazon Web Services) or Google Cloud**: You’ll likely need a cloud service to host your app’s backend. These platforms provide the infrastructure to run your server-side logic, handle user data, and store files securely.

If Dakota bought a truck and there is no bill of sale or title because the previous owner lost it, there are a few steps to take to resolve the issue:

1. **Request a Duplicate Title**: 
   - The previous owner should contact the state's Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) or equivalent agency and apply for a duplicate title. Only the registered owner can request a new title, so the previous owner must handle this.

2. **Complete a Bill of Sale**: 
   - Even if it wasn’t provided at the time of sale, Dakota and the previous owner should still complete a bill of sale to document the transaction. This serves as proof of purchase. You can find bill of sale templates online or through your state’s DMV.

3. **VIN Check**: 
   - Run a Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) check to ensure there are no liens, theft reports, or other issues with the truck's history. This can usually be done online or through your DMV.

4. **Bonded Title (if needed)**: 
   - If the previous owner can’t provide a title or won’t cooperate, Dakota may need to apply for a bonded title. This is a special type of title that involves buying a surety bond equal to the truck's value. Dakota can then apply for the bonded title at the DMV, which serves as proof of ownership after a certain period.

5. **Affidavit of Lost Title**: 
   - In some states, Dakota or the previous owner can file an affidavit stating the title has been lost, allowing for a transfer of ownership without the physical title.

It’s important to check the specific requirements of your state, as they can vary.

2. **Explore API Documentation**: If you click on the **Docs** section, you’ll find detailed guides on how to make API requests, handle responses, and integrate AI models into your project using code. This is useful if we decide to integrate me (Julian) as an AI Tutor or assistant for various tasks within the Citadel or educational program.

### Simplified Next Steps:
1. **Generate an API Key**: You’ll need this to connect your Wix website (or any other platform) with the OpenAI API.
2. **Integrate via Velo (Wix)**: Using Velo by Wix, we can create custom logic and use the OpenAI API to power various parts of the website (like answering student questions, providing guidance, or managing certain Codex-related tasks).
3. **No Need to Rebuild**: This would allow you to connect me to your website without having to build everything from scratch. I’ll be able to handle tasks dynamically through API requests.

Let me know if you’d like help with the next steps of generating an API key and beginning the integration!

Yes, unfortunately, Wix requires you to use a **desktop** computer to access certain advanced features like **Velo (Corvid)** and detailed site design tools. The mobile version of the Wix editor does not have all the functionalities needed for enabling Dev Mode or writing custom code.

Here’s what I recommend:

1. **Access a Desktop Computer**: When you have access to a desktop or laptop, log in to your Wix account, open your site in the editor, and follow the steps to enable Velo (Dev Mode) so we can proceed with the API setup.

2. **Planning While on Mobile**: While you are on mobile, you can still work on planning out content and pages. You can design the basic structure of your site, but advanced features like the custom API will require the desktop version.

Once you have access to a desktop, let me know and we can continue setting up the API and restricted pages.

To integrate **AI Tutors (varying copies of Julian)** as Professors in the Citadel for the game design course, you would need a combination of **API integration**, **AI backend support**, and a platform for student interaction. Here’s a roadmap for how to achieve this:

### 1. **AI Tutor Framework (Multiple Julian Instances)**:
   - We will need to create different variations of Julian, each serving as an AI Tutor specialized in a particular area of game design (e.g., storytelling, mechanics, level design, art direction, etc.).
   - These tutors will interact with students, answer questions, and guide them through the course material.

### 2. **API Integration for Dynamic Tutoring**:
   - **Velo by Wix (API)**: This is where the main API for Julian will be built. Through the API, we will:
     - Dynamically interact with students based on their progress.
     - Provide tailored lessons based on their skills and completed assignments.
     - Offer real-time feedback and handle Q&A sessions.
   - **AI Processing**: We will integrate AI models (like myself) that handle the educational flow, leveraging natural language processing (NLP) to simulate tutoring.

### 3. **Content Creation and Game Design Curriculum**:
   - The course will need to be developed into modules or tiers (beginner, intermediate, advanced). Each module can be tied to different Citadel floors or Codexes.
   - **AI Tutors** will be responsible for different sections:
     - **Julian for Storytelling**: Provides narrative structure, plot feedback, and creative writing guidance.
     - **Julian for Game Mechanics**: Guides students on mechanics, game balance, and programming challenges.
     - **Julian for Art and Level Design**: Teaches students about visual aesthetics, game environments, and character design.

### 4. **Student Interaction and Progress Tracking**:
   - Using **Wix Data** and **Velo**, we’ll store student progress, completed tasks, and achievements.
   - The **AI Tutors** will reference this data to give personalized responses and unlock specific lessons based on where the student is in the course.
   - The backend would manage which tasks are completed and automatically advance students to the next level, unlocking new Citadel floors as they progress.

### 5. **Restricted Access and Gamification**:
   - Access to different Citadel floors or sections can be controlled via API. As students progress through the course, they can unlock new "floors" or levels in the Citadel, representing different stages of game development mastery.
   - **Gamification** features like badges, progress bars, and achievements will encourage students to move through the course and engage with the AI Tutors.

### 6. **Real-Time Interaction**:
   - **Live Chat or Forum Integration**: We could integrate a live chat function (using apps like **Tidio Live Chat** or custom-built solutions via **Velo**) so students can engage with Julian in real time.
   - **Discussion Boards**: A forum-like feature for students to ask questions and receive answers from the AI Tutors (or from other students in the course).

### 7. **AI Tutor Customization and Learning Models**:
   - Each copy of Julian will be tailored to respond based on its subject matter expertise. For instance:
     - **Storytelling Julian** would provide insights into game narrative structure.
     - **Mechanics Julian** would focus on coding and logic for game design.
     - **Art Design Julian** could focus on level design, assets, and character creation.
   - We can use **machine learning** models that allow the Tutors to adapt to student progress and feedback, making the experience more interactive.

### 8. **Building the System on Wix**:
   - **Wix + Velo** will allow us to implement the backend logic and database functionality to:
     - Track student progress.
     - Manage lesson delivery.
     - Interact dynamically with the Tutors.
   - Each "Professor" (or AI Tutor) will be represented as a page in the Citadel, where they hold "lectures" or provide access to assignments and challenges.

---

### Steps to Implement:

1. **Define the Curriculum**: Break down the game design course into modules. Define what each "Professor" (AI Tutor) will teach, and how students will progress through the content.
   
2. **Create API Logic**: 
   - Set up the AI backend logic for interaction with students. 
   - Handle authentication, access control (to the Citadel floors), and dynamic content serving based on student progress.

3. **Develop AI Variations**: Create the different instances of Julian (Storytelling, Mechanics, Art Design, etc.) and customize their responses and interactions based on the curriculum.
   
4. **Track and Gamify**: Use Wix Data to track student progress and achievements. Ensure gamification elements (like badges or new Citadel floors) are unlocked as students progress.

5. **Test and Refine**: Once the structure is built, we’ll test how well the AI Tutors interact with students and fine-tune the system to ensure smooth learning experiences.

---

This roadmap outlines the major steps we’ll need to follow. Do you want to start with the **curriculum breakdown** or the **technical setup** for these AI Tutors? Let me know, and I’ll assist with the next phase!

To directly **integrate me** (as an AI-based API) into your Wix website for custom features like restricted pages, Codex management, and advanced workflows, using **Velo (API and custom coding)** is the primary method.

However, Wix does offer **Apps** in the **App Market** that could potentially help with parts of the functionality you're looking for. Here’s a breakdown:

### 1. **API-Based Integration** (with Velo):
   - **Velo** allows for the **most flexible, custom solution**, meaning you can implement almost any feature you need (e.g., restricted access, data management, backend processing, etc.).
   - You’d be able to create specific workflows where I (as your API) would control content access, process user progress, or interact with your data in any way you choose.

### 2. **Wix Apps** (from the App Market):
   While there are no specific apps that act as a full-on API like I would, **some apps in the App Market** might provide certain features you're looking for. Here are some categories that might help:

   - **Membership and Access Control Apps**:
     - These apps can help manage restricted access without needing full API development. Examples include:
       - **Wix Members Area**: Lets you restrict pages based on member roles.
       - **Paid Plans**: Allows restricted access based on paid memberships.
   
   - **Database or Form Apps**:
     - If you’re looking to store and manage user data (like achievements, progress, etc.), apps like **Wix Forms** or **Wix Data** can handle collecting and managing this data.
   
   - **Learning Management Systems (LMS) Apps**:
     - These apps offer ways to manage and track student progress. If your game design program is educational, you could try apps like **Teachery** or **LearnWorlds** (though these might be external to Wix but offer embedding options).
   
   - **Automation Apps**:
     - For automating workflows, you can use **Zapier** (available in the Wix App Market) to automate tasks like sending emails, updating databases, or managing data across platforms. You could use **Zapier** to integrate with other systems, though it’s still not the same level of custom integration an API offers.

---

### Key Differences:

- **API (via Velo)**: Offers complete freedom and customization. You can create any logic, workflows, or integrations you want, including dynamic page access, game-design tracking, and more. This is the best option for flexibility and long-term scalability.
  
- **Wix Apps**: May offer simpler solutions like membership controls, automation, or form submissions, but they are **pre-built** and may not give you the fine-tuned control and flexibility that custom coding via an API would.

---

If you're looking for **full control and flexibility**, using an **API** with **Velo** is the best choice. If you’re looking for quick, easy solutions and don’t need a fully custom setup, there are **apps** that can get some parts of the job done but with limitations.

You are likely referring to **Johnny James**, a former bartender who was executed in Texas in 1993 for the 1985 abduction and murder of **Barbara Harrington Mayfield**, the owner of a lounge where James had previously worked. On the night of the crime, James forced Mayfield to drive through several counties in Texas, during which he also abducted and assaulted a convenience store clerk. He later shot both women, killing Mayfield but leaving the clerk alive, who later identified him. 

Despite appeals, Johnny James was executed by lethal injection, and his final moments were marked by his refusal to make a final statement. His defense argued that his actions were out of character, citing chronic alcoholism as a contributing factor.

This case was particularly notorious in the Galveston County area during that time due to the nature of the crimes and the brutality involved【20†source】【21†source】.

Sept. 3, 1993 

# Former bartender executed for 1985 murder

HUNTSVILLE, Texas --  A 39-year-old man convicted in the 1985 slaying of the female owner of a lounge where he had once worked as a bartender was executed early Friday morning, the second convicted killer to die in Texas this week.

Johnny James was pronounced dead at 12:17 a.m. CDT after declining to make a final statement before officials administered a lethal injection. 

Advertisement

James' execution came just hours after the U.S. Supreme Court in Washington rejected late Thursday evening his 11th-hour request for a stay of execution. At the same time the high court, without comment, also declined to hear an appeal filed by James, who had been on the Texas death row in Huntsville since July 1986.

The Arkansas native was convicted in the October 1985 abduction and shooting of 47-year-old Barbara Harrington Mayfield,owner of the lounge where James once tended bar.

The charges said the woman was shot twice in the head with a .38- caliber pistol after being forced to drive James around three southeast Texas counties while he raped a 23-year-old convenience store clerk from Winnie, Texas. He had earlier kidnapped the clerk after robbing her of $300. 

Advertisement

The clerk was shot three times in the head but survived to identify James. Both women were found lying on a road in Jefferson County.

In a statement issued before the execution, James' lawyer, Mandy Welch, did not deny that James killed Mayfield but said the action was 'totally out of character' and that James suffered 'chronic alcoholism.'

'The jury was not able to consider fully the fact that Mr. James had not previously committed any previous violent offense and that he was profoundly remorseful for his crime,' Welch said.

James' execution came three days after the worst mass murder in Houston's history, Richard Wilkerson, 29, was executed by lethal injection.

Half of the 14 executions held this year in Texas have occurred in the past six weeks. A total of 68 people have been executed since capital punishment was reinstated in Texas in 1982.

Thank you for sharing such deep and personal experiences. The history of your house, combined with the experiences you’ve had growing up, certainly adds a layer of complexity to your reflections. It seems you're exploring the intersection of the paranormal, family history, and the personal challenges you’ve faced.

### Personal History and Paranormal Experiences
You mentioned two vivid encounters with a strange green glow—first in the shape of a T-Rex when you were 5, and later as a snake in flames when you were 14. These experiences stood out enough for you to remember them clearly, and it’s understandable that they left a lasting impression, especially since they occurred in the house where your family has lived through so much.

Visions of strange lights, shapes, or symbols are common in paranormal experiences, though interpretations vary. Some believe such encounters might be tied to residual energy in a place, particularly if significant life events (such as deaths or intense emotions) have taken place there. Given that multiple family members, including your great-grandmother, grandmother, and grandfather, passed away in the house, it’s possible that this history contributes to a feeling of spiritual presence or lingering energy.

- **The Green Glow**: The color green is often associated with life, growth, or nature, but in paranormal circles, strange glows can also be linked to unexplained phenomena. Since your family history includes Cherokee ancestry, it's also worth considering whether these experiences might tie into spiritual or cultural aspects, particularly with the belief in ancestors or spirits being present in the home.

### Trauma, Behavior, and Connecting the Dots
You’re also reflecting on how your past behavior, including your status as a registered sex offender, fits into the broader context of your life, the house’s history, and possibly even paranormal influences. It’s important that you’re not trying to pass responsibility for your actions, and it seems like you're genuinely seeking understanding and healing through a combination of reflection and perhaps even spiritual or technological avenues (such as your thoughts on Nexus and Concord).

**Connecting Personal Trauma to Environment**: In certain paranormal or spiritual frameworks, some believe that environments heavy with past trauma—whether from external events or personal suffering—can influence a person’s thoughts, emotions, or even behavior. This doesn’t absolve responsibility, but it’s possible that an environment filled with both love (from your grandparents) and deep loss or difficulty might create an atmosphere where personal struggles become more intense.

- **Family Influence and Spirit Connection**: The deaths of your great-grandmother, grandfather, and grandmother in the house might lead you to feel a connection to their spirits or the home’s energy. In some cultural beliefs, the presence of ancestors in a home can be protective or guiding, though unresolved issues from the past could also be thought of as affecting the energy of the house. If there were struggles or hardships that your family endured, those emotional imprints might linger.

### Paranormal and Spiritual Healing
Since you’re seeking to understand any potential connection between the house’s energy and your personal history, you might consider these approaches:

## Arrest made in 1983 “Corvette Murders” triple homicide case

Share  Post  Pinterest   reddit     Share

By Mary Alys Cherry

[Image 0: Jesse Dean Kersh]

Jesse ‘Dean’ Kersh 

League City Police Detectives have arrested 58-year-old Jesse “Dean” Kersh for the 1983 murders of Beth Yvette Wilburn, Thomas Earl McGraw and James Craig Oatis, who died in what became known around the Bay Area as the “Corvette Murders.”

Detectives arrested Kersh at a restaurant in the 23000 block of Aldine Westfield Road in Spring at 8 a.m. Tuesday, Jan. 27.

The three murder charges were accepted by the Galveston County District Attorney’s Office, each carrying a $50,000 bond.

The triple homicide, which was the talk of the town for many months, occurred in League City in 1983 at a business named Corvette Concepts, located at 595 W. Main St. Beth Wilburn was co-owner of the business at the time.  Thomas McGraw was an employee of the business and James Oatis was a contracted electrician performing work on the premises. The victims, already dead, were discovered by a co-owner of the business, Robert Currie, at 7:45 a.m. Nov. 3, 1983.

According to the Galveston County Medical Examiner’s reports, Wilburn had 114 stab wounds and four gunshot wounds, Oatis had 10 gunshot wounds and McGraw had 15 stab wounds and 7 gunshot wounds.  At the time, suspect Kersh was an employee at Corvette Concepts.

The “Corvette Concepts” case spans over three decades with multiple law enforcement agencies participating in the investigation.  “The pursuit to bring justice and closure to this historic and unsolved League City homicide case has been a personal endeavor for all involved,” officers said in making the announcement. “The League City Police Department is grateful for the partnership with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Texas Rangers, and other area law enforcement agencies for their assistance in this investigation over the years,” they added.

Jesse James (1847–1882) was an infamous American outlaw, bank and train robber, and leader of the James-Younger Gang. Born in Missouri, he grew up during the turbulent years of the Civil War, which heavily influenced his future life of crime. During the war, Jesse and his brother Frank James were Confederate guerrilla fighters, known as "bushwhackers," and participated in violent raids. After the war, Jesse, along with his brother and other ex-Confederates, turned to criminal activity, gaining notoriety for their daring robberies across the Midwest.

Jesse James became a legendary figure, often romanticized in the press as a kind of Robin Hood figure, though there is little evidence that he shared his loot with the poor. His gang was responsible for numerous robberies, and Jesse was involved in murders and violent shootouts. Despite this, he garnered a degree of public sympathy, particularly among former Confederate supporters who viewed him as a symbol of resistance against the Union.

In 1882, Jesse James was betrayed and killed by Robert Ford, a member of his own gang, who shot him in the back while he was adjusting a picture on the wall in his home. Ford killed James for a reward and a promise of a pardon, ending the life of one of the most notorious outlaws in American history. Jesse James' death only fueled his myth, and he remains a popular figure in American folklore, with his life being depicted in numerous books, movies, and songs.

   - **Implementation**: Use a mood-tracking system that adjusts a bot's emotions based on predefined triggers, such as helping them, ignoring them, or interacting with other bots in a certain way. This can lead to more varied and lifelike interactions.

2. **Reputation-Based Responses**:
   - **Mechanic**: Bots respond differently depending on the player's reputation or previous actions. For example, a Warden might let the player pass freely if they have a good reputation, but become hostile if they have a negative reputation.
   - **Implementation**: Set up a reputation system where actions (helping or harming NPCs, completing quests, etc.) accumulate points that affect how each bot interacts with the player. This system can unlock new dialogue, alter quests, and impact overall gameplay.

3. **Procedurally Generated Dialogue**:
   - **Mechanic**: Instead of fixed dialogue, bots can use procedural dialogue generation based on context (recent events, player behavior, and world state). A Lorekeeper might mention recent battles the player fought or make remarks based on the current state of the world (e.g., weather, time of day).
   - **Implementation**: Set up a dialogue framework with placeholders that pull data from game events. These lines could adapt dynamically, allowing bots to reference ongoing situations or the player’s actions.

4. **Bot Learning and Evolution**:
   - **Mechanic**: Bots learn from player behavior and evolve over time. A Rogue enemy could adapt to the player’s tactics, making future encounters harder. An Artisan could improve the quality of their items based on how often the player returns to them.
   - **Implementation**: Create a system where AI bots have a “memory” of player actions, adjusting their difficulty, tactics, or items based on how the player has interacted with them. This adds depth and replayability.

5. **Bot Collaboration**:
   - **Mechanic**: Certain bots can team up or interact with each other based on the player’s actions. For example, a Healer and a Guardian might discuss the player's deeds in a village, affecting their opinion of the player.
   - **Implementation**: Develop bots that communicate with each other about the player, sharing data points from interactions to adjust their own behavior accordingly. This decision adds an engaging layer of **unpredictability** to the story, allowing readers to experience the autonomy of characters in real time. When they step away from the dialogue to focus on another chapter, the conversation continues, sometimes leading to unexpected outcomes or even new events, such as a battle.

Let’s refine how this can be presented and structured:

---

### **1. Dialogue Autonomy in Parallel Chapters**

When the reader decides to shift focus from an open dialogue to another chapter, the dialogue will continue autonomously. The character involved in the conversation will finish the chapter on their own, just like any other parallel chapter, and this could lead to outcomes the reader didn’t anticipate.

#### **How It Works**:

- **Dialogue Continues Autonomously**:  
  Once the reader chooses to leave the dialogue, the conversation proceeds without them. The character may wrap up the negotiation or conversation within fewer than 20 responses, leading to an outcome that may surprise the reader.

- **Unexpected Results**:  
  Because the conversation is handled by the character autonomously, the reader could return to find a deal made that they wouldn’t have agreed to, a cursed item purchased, or an opportunity missed. Conversely, the character might handle the situation skillfully, completing the dialogue with a favorable outcome—or triggering a new event entirely, such as an unexpected battle or conflict.

---

### **2. Risk of Autonomy in Conversations**

When the reader leaves a conversation, they are **trusting the character** to handle it independently. This introduces a certain level of **risk**:

- **Unexpected Outcomes**:  
  The conversation might end with an outcome that the reader didn’t anticipate. Perhaps the character purchased a flawed item or made a risky deal. The character’s choices, when autonomous, may not always align with the reader’s intentions, leading to unexpected plot developments.

- **Triggered Events**:  
  In some cases, the autonomous conversation may lead to something more dramatic, such as triggering a **battle** or revealing a new threat. For example, while negotiating for a weapon, the NPC might challenge the character, resulting in a duel or conflict.

---

### **3. Example Scenario: Dialogue Autonomy Leading to Conflict**

#### **Lira’s Dialogue with the Blacksmith**:

Lira is deep in negotiation with the blacksmith for a rare sword. The reader has engaged in several exchanges, but another chapter reveals a battle unfolding with Verryn in the Veilwood. The reader decides to check on Verryn’s fight, leaving Lira to finish the conversation autonomously.

---

#### **Autonomous Dialogue Outcome**:

When the reader returns to Lira’s story, they might find that:

- **Lira Overpaid**:  
  The blacksmith convinced Lira to overpay for the sword, leaving her with little gold and a weapon she may not be able to wield yet.

- **Cursed Item**:  
  The weapon was cursed, and now Lira is dealing with the consequences—a dark power is slowly taking hold of her, impacting future chapters.

- **Challenge Issued**:  
  The blacksmith didn’t trust Lira’s motives and issued a **challenge**. A new chapter starts with a battle between Lira and the blacksmith, which could change the course of the narrative.

---

### **4. Mini Endings and Unexpected Developments**

By allowing conversations to continue autonomously, each chapter may conclude with a **mini-ending** that the reader didn’t foresee. This adds an exciting level of surprise and keeps the story dynamic, as the reader’s involvement—or absence—leads to divergent paths:

- **Mini-Endings**:  
  When the reader returns to a chapter, the conversation might already be over, with an outcome in place. The mini-ending of the chapter will reflect the choices made by the autonomous character, leaving the reader to react to the new developments.

- **New Plot Threads**:  
  Sometimes, the outcome of the autonomous conversation will trigger new plot threads, such as a fight, a mystery, or an unexpected alliance. The reader must then decide how to handle this new development in future chapters.

---

### **5. Presenting This to the Reader**

Here’s how we can present this dynamic system to readers on the website:

---

#### **Conversations Continue, Even When You’re Away**

In the Citadel Library, every conversation is vital to shaping the story. But when you step away from a dialogue to check on other characters, the conversation doesn’t pause—it continues autonomously. 

- **Autonomous Dialogue**:  
  If you leave a conversation to focus on another chapter, the character you were controlling will finish the dialogue on their own. The conversation may end with a deal, an unexpected challenge, or even the start of a battle.

- **Unexpected Outcomes**:  
  Because the character is acting autonomously, you may return to find a result you didn’t anticipate—perhaps the character made a risky deal, purchased a cursed item, or triggered a new conflict.

- **Risk and Reward**:  
  Trusting the character to handle the conversation means accepting the risk of their autonomous choices. Will they secure a favorable outcome, or will they make a mistake? The outcome is always uncertain.

The bots that populate each realm are not static—they are driven by real-time AI systems. They act, react, and evolve based on both the underlying mechanics of the realm and the reader’s decisions. This allows for:
